title: Affine-space purity
statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], put
$\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$ with $n\geq1$, and assume
$e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$, as in [def-pur-affine-line-datum].
Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let $d\geq0$, and let
$K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. The comparison

$$
\gamma_{p_d,K}:Lp_d^*K(d)[2d]\longrightarrow Rp_d^!K
$$

of [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Induct on the affine dimension with the claim quantified over every separated finite-type $k$-scheme $T$ in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison] and every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, with the fixed finite coefficient ring $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, and $e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\mid n$. For every such $T$, the standard affine line, zero section, coordinate and punctured complement form the datum of [def-pur-affine-line-datum], with the same integer $N=n/e(E/\mathbf Q_\ell)\geq1$. Thus the affine-line theorem is applicable over every base quantified over in the induction. At dimension zero the definition gives $p_0=\mathrm{id}_T$ and $\gamma_{p_0,M}=\mathrm{id}_M$. At dimension one the ordered composite has one affine-line factor; the identity composition, pullback and twist unit identifications in that definition identify it with $\gamma_{p_1,M}$ of [thm-pur-affine-line-purity]. Thus the claim holds in dimensions zero and one.

source.place: induction paragraph, with dimensions 0 and 1 separated to meet the positive-block hypotheses

proof.text:
Let $d\geq2$ and assume the claim in dimension $d-1$ for every such base and input. Put $T=\mathbf A^1_Y$, let $p:T\to Y$ be its projection, and let $q:\mathbf A^{d-1}_T\to T$ be the projection, so $pq=p_d$ under the ordered coordinate identification in [prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law]. The schemes and projections are separated finite type as specified in [def-pur-affine-space-comparison]; on affine charts they are polynomial algebras and their diagonals are cut out by coordinate differences. Apply clause (2) of [thm-sf-preservation-class] to $p$ to obtain $M=Rp^!K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$. The universally quantified induction hypothesis therefore gives that $\gamma_{q,M}$ is an isomorphism, while the fixed divisibility hypothesis supplies the affine-line datum over $Y$ by [def-pur-affine-line-datum], so [thm-pur-affine-line-purity] gives that $\gamma_{p,K}$ is an isomorphism. Both block lengths $d-1$ and $1$ are positive, so [prop-pur-affine-space-composition-law] gives, after its specified source reassociation $J$,
$$
\gamma_{p_d,K}=c_{p,q}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{q,M}\circ\bigl(Lq^*(\gamma_{p,K})(d-1)[2d-2]\bigr)\circ J.
$$
The third factor has inverse $Lq^*(\gamma_{p,K}^{-1})(d-1)[2d-2]$, because a functor preserves the two inverse equations. The other factors are the isomorphisms $c_{p,q}^{-1}$, $\gamma_{q,M}$ and $J$. Composing their inverses in reverse order supplies an inverse to the displayed map. This proves the induction step and hence the assertion for all $d\geq0$.

source.place: induction paragraph, block lengths d-1 and 1; domain of the induction input made explicit

proof_origin.place: induction paragraph (base cases and domains expanded)
